name: Hassan Tower
hero_subtitle: The unfinished minaret that still defines Rabat’s skyline.

overview.title: An Almohad ambition left open to the sky
overview.p1: Hassan Tower was meant to anchor one of the largest mosques of the Almohad age. The minaret rose; the prayer hall columns never fully became a finished mosque. What remains is one of Morocco’s most recognisable silhouettes.
overview.p2: You walk the esplanade among the column stumps, look up at the tower’s carved faces, and understand the scale the builders intended. The site is open, windy and inseparable from the neighbouring Mohammed V Mausoleum.
overview.p3: Visit in the morning if you want softer light on the stone, or late day when the tower catches warmer colour. Guard changing and formal visits nearby can draw crowds — check the rhythm of the mausoleum if you plan both.

q1.question: Can I climb Hassan Tower?
q1.answer: No. The minaret is not open for climbing; you experience it from the esplanade.

q2.question: Is there a ticket?
q2.answer: The esplanade is generally free to walk; the mausoleum next door follows its own entry rules and dress expectations.

q3.question: How much time do I need?
q3.answer: Thirty to sixty minutes for the tower and columns; add time if you enter the mausoleum.

q4.question: Is it far from the kasbah?
q4.answer: A short taxi or a longer walk — many visitors do kasbah in the morning and Hassan Tower after lunch.

q5.question: Best photos?
q5.answer: Morning side light or late afternoon colour on the stone; midday is harsher and busier.

food.title: Eat before or after on the avenues
food.p1: There is no dining on the esplanade itself. Plan coffee or lunch in the surrounding avenues or back toward the medina and ville nouvelle.
food.p2: Treat Hassan Tower as a monument stop, not a food stop.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Hassan Tower

1.title: Read the unfinished plan on the ground
1.desc: Walk the full rectangle of columns before focusing only on the tower. The empty footprint explains the ambition better than any single photo of the minaret. Closed shoes help on uneven stone.

2.title: Coordinate with the Mausoleum schedule
2.desc: The two sites sit together. Modest dress is essential if you enter the mausoleum. Guard ceremonies and peak tour times can cluster midday — arrive earlier for a calmer esplanade.

3.title: Wind, sun and open space
3.desc: There is little shade on the esplanade. Bring water, a hat in summer, and a light layer when the Atlantic wind picks up. Keep valuables close; it is a major tourist node with pickpocket risk in dense groups.
